messages.content: my neighbor asked to use my camera tomorrow. i need it myself. help me say no in a kind way.
i am sorry, but i need my camera tomorrow and cannot give it to you then.
i do not want to say sorry. can it still be kind?
yes. you can say: thanks for asking, but i need my camera tomorrow. i hope you find another one you can use.
please do not add that i can give it to them later. i have not chosen that.
thanks for asking, but i need my camera tomorrow and cannot give it to you then.
would it be better to say maybe, so they do not feel sad?
if you already know that your answer is no, maybe could leave them waiting for a different answer. a clear no can help them make another plan.
what if they ask why i need it?
you can give a short reason if you want to, but you do not have to tell them every detail. you could say: i already have a plan to use it tomorrow.
put that together with the answer, without saying thanks again.
i already have a plan to use my camera tomorrow, so i cannot give it to you then.
that is enough.
okay. that message gives your answer and your reason clearly.
write a quiet story about two friends walking without much talking.

two friends met outside after a long day. one had many things on her mind, but she did not want to explain them all. the other asked whether she wanted to talk or just walk. she chose to walk. they went slowly through the park, looking at the trees and the people going home. after a while, she began to tell him about her day. he listened without asking her to speak fast. when they returned, her day was still hard, but she no longer felt so alone with it.
why did he not ask more questions at first?
he gave her a choice about whether to talk or just walk. when she chose walking, he did not ask her about every part of her day. he let her choose when to start talking.
does the story say he fixed everything?
no. it says her day was still hard. his help was being there and listening, rather than making every problem go away.
write one thing she might say near the end.
thank you for walking with me. i did not know how to start talking, and it helped that i did not have to start right away.
how could he answer without making it about himself?
i am happy you came. we can walk again another day if you would like.
can that last sentence leave her free to say no?
yes. if you would like makes it a choice for her. it does not say that she must walk with him again.
the kitchen door is open. the bedroom door was open this morning. are they both open now?
we know that the kitchen door is open now. we only know that the bedroom door was open this morning. it may still be open, but your message does not tell us that for sure.
why not just say yes?
because that would add information you did not give. something that was true this morning does not always stay true all day.
what if nobody has been in the bedroom after this morning?
that gives us more information, but it still does not tell us for sure that the door is open. for example, someone could close a door from outside the room. we would need more information or a check.
i just checked. the bedroom door is closed.
then the kitchen door is open and the bedroom door is closed, from the information you have given.
which sentence should i use to tell my father?
the kitchen door is open, but the bedroom door is closed.
what did the word but add there?
it helps point out the difference between the kitchen door and the bedroom door. you could use and too, but but helps make that difference more clear.
can you make that explanation shorter?
but helps make the difference clear: one door is open while the other is closed.
change this to two children: the child has a book and is reading near the window.
the children have a book and are reading near the window.
why did you not write books?
two children can read one book together. changing the number of children does not by itself change the number of books. i kept your one book.
now give each child a different book.
the children each have a book and are reading near the window.
is each child have a book correct?
use each child has a book. each child is about one child at a time, so has goes with it.
but you used have after each before.

yes. in the children each have a book, the sentence starts with the children, which is more than one child. in each child has a book, it starts with each child. that difference helps explain why have is correct in one sentence and has is correct in the other.
give both correct sentences together.
each child has a book. the children each have a book.
make the first one about yesterday.
each child had a book yesterday.
i want to return a book and buy bread after work. the library is near my office and the shop is near my home. what is a simple plan?

you could return the book after work, then go home and buy bread at the shop on your way. the library is near your office, and the shop is near home, so you would not have to go back near the office later.
i just learned that the library closes before i finish work.
then returning the book after work will not work that day. can you go before work, during a break, or on another day when it is open?
i have a free morning tomorrow. i still need bread today.
you could buy bread on your way home today, then return the book tomorrow morning. you would get the food you need today and leave the library visit until tomorrow.
why did you change your first plan?
you gave a new fact about when the library closes. a plan should change when new information makes an important part of it impossible.
can you give the new plan as a message to myself?
today, buy bread on the way home. tomorrow morning, return the book to the library.
should you say what time the library opens?
i do not know that from your messages. check its opening time before you go, rather than using a time i make up.
that is all i needed.
you are welcome. the new plan leaves the library visit for your free morning.
write a story about a child finding a page that looks empty on one side.

a child found a page on the floor next to the table. the side he could see was empty, so he thought he could use it for a drawing. before he started, he turned it over. there was a letter on the other side. he asked his mother whose letter it was. she said it was a letter she had written to his grandmother and had not sent yet. he gave it back to her and found another page for his drawing.
was the page empty?
one side was empty, but the other side had a letter on it. saying that the whole page was empty would leave out an important detail.
why did he not draw on the letter?
he turned the page over before using it and asked his mother about the writing.
could the story end with his mother helping him find paper?
yes. she could thank him for taking care and give him a clean page from the desk. then he could draw while she finished her letter.
write her thank you in one sentence.
thank you for looking at the other side and asking me before using the page.
what would be too much to say about this child from one story?
it would be too much to say that he always looks at every detail or never does anything wrong. this story gives us one example of him taking care before using a page.
please make that answer shorter.
the story gives one example of him taking care. it does not tell us what he always does.
